title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_89.txt
concise_summary: PKD develops a theology of resurrection as alchemical transmutation, using his short story 'The Man Who Knew How to Lose' as a template to decode the Gospels. He proposes that the Kingdom operates through paradoxical logic where one must already be inside to enter, and introduces a 'time cube' where 45 AD and 1974 AD coexist, requiring non-linear reasoning (heuristics) to access. The future contains and retrieves the past; resurrection is not biological but a secret process transmuting base metal into gold.
key_claims: Resurrection is not the biological return of the dead but a secret alchemical transmutation process in which the lowest (degraded matter/base metal) is instantaneously transformed into the highest form
The Gospel/New Testament is an occult alchemical text encoding instructions for spiritual resurrection as coded language, analogous to the Bardo Thodol, not a historical narrative of Jesus
The Kingdom paradox: entrance is inside the Kingdom (anamnesis, not discovery); one must already be in to enter; non-linear reasoning (heuristics) replaces cause-to-effect logic
Time collapses from linear sequence into a cube where 45 AD and 1974 AD are equally present; the future retrieves/contains the past; effect can exist within cause
Stories function as codebooks/neutral grids decoding complex reality; PKD's fiction (Ubik, The Man Who Knew How to Lose) contains the theological/spiritual truth it portrays
Spiritual choice (accepting Fox/divine) determines spiritual life-or-death; rejecting the spiritual for the material is self-negating spiritual death

tensions: Jesus is claimed not to have existed historically, yet Christ is the operative spiritual principle of resurrection—unresolved boundary between myth and fact
PKD insists resurrection breaks out unexpectedly and cannot be controlled, yet simultaneously claims the Gospels provide an accurate (if not formulaic) guide to it
The story decodes reality exactly, yet PKD admits he did not intend the final message—how can non-intentional art be a reliable codebook?
Time is described as a cube where all moments are equally present, yet PKD still speaks of future retrieving past—spatial and temporal language conflict
Spiritual life/death are the stakes, yet the example turns on whether a physical cure (Rybus' health) validates Fox's spiritual claim
PKD needs anamnesis (remembering) to access the Kingdom, but the Kingdom is supposedly already-present and invisible—how does memory bridge this?
Laws of physics degrade and compress matter, yet resurrection claims to transmute base matter into highest form—contradiction with entropy?
